text: You could never buy the Eiffel Tower.
In 1925, one man lost a fortune trying.
The tower was only meant to stand 20 years.
By 1925, it was rusting and costly.
So con man Victor Lustig got fake government letterhead
and invited scrap dealers to a luxury hotel.
The state will sell the tower for scrap.
But wouldn't the buyer just go to the police?
Dealer André Poisson paid, plus a bribe, and Lustig vanished with the cash.
And that's not even the craziest part.
Poisson was too embarrassed to report it, so Lustig came back and tried to sell it again.
He never sold a tower, he sold the buyer's silence.
Is the Taj Mahal still available?
Comment, would you have told the police?
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
